analysis.title: Hedge Funds Defensive / Hawkish Fedspeak Continues / UK Data / Japan Inflation / US-Iran
key_insights: UBS Prime Brokerage shows hedge funds stayed defensive in the US and Europe after NVDA earnings. Health Care/Pharma was the most net bought in both regions, while selling hit high-momentum Semis and Hyperscalers in the US and Industrials in Europe.
US gross exposure was broadly unchanged and European funds added +1% to GMV. Prime book and client talks show little appetite to re-gross into year-end given tough performance.
Retail, CTAs and Long-Onlys show limited buying appetite, in contrast with the summer when Long-Only buying helped sustain the August rebound.

Net exposure to Software has surpassed Semis for the first time this year and is back to the 2024/5 average. Semis/Software correlation flipped firmly positive this month, and HFs net sold Semis (-0.4std) this week.

Fedspeak stayed hawkish. Paulson said more tightening is needed, Goolsbee said 'everything is on the table' for December, and Barr called financial conditions 'quite accommodative'. Markets price a 25bp hike at the Dec. 9 FOMC with near-certainty.
Treasuries are on track for a fifth straight session of gains, the longest rally since late June, as equity risk-off haven demand temporarily overwhelms the hawkish rate signal.
UK October PSNB was £17bn vs £18bn Bloomberg consensus. Debt interest costs rose to £11.2bn, RPI hit 4.2% and is forecast above 5% early next year, so the fiscal backdrop stays tight.
UK October retail sales beat widely, +0.7% m/m incl fuel vs 0.0% est, and GfK confidence rose 2 points to -22.
Japan October CPI missed on all three measures, with headline 2.3% y/y vs 2.5% est.
Trump told Axios he will delay any decision on further Iran strikes until the new year. WTI is near $83 and Brent near $92, both down about 5% on the week, for a third weekly drop.
SpaceX sold $32bn of debt at 8.25% while rated BBB, versus 5.70% for the BBB sector average. The note argues tech issuance is crowding out the rest of credit rather than Treasuries.
TAIEX fell 6.23% Friday and 17.5% on the week, its worst week since 1991, led by TSMC (44% index weight) down about 15% on the week.

UK PM Burnham meets EU leaders on a reset covering agri-food, carbon markets and youth mobility, which he said could add about 0.4% to UK GDP. Financial services alignment and China policy remain fault lines.
US Congress is preparing a bipartisan bill to ban Chinese car sales in the US, during Trump-Xi talks in Shenzhen.
LME 3M copper fell over 7% in two days to the lowest since April. UBS CIO stays constructive and keeps a $15,500/mt forecast by mid-2027.

Equities: MSCI ACWI is on a seven-day losing streak, its worst since 2023, with 92% of S&P constituents falling and VIX at 29. The UBS AI Winners basket is back to Midterm lows, down 4%. HF and systematic positioning is now very short.
TYZ6 is back above 106 on volume near double average, and SFRZ6 is up 1.75 ticks. Positioning is not overly long, so UBS sees room to rally, but inflation fears cap the upside.

EURUSD holds firm, testing 1.1010 and 1.0970. A break below 1.0950 is needed for more downside and a move above 1.1020 would ease downside risk. Precious metals are pressured by hawkish Fed and the equity sell-off.

risk_factors: Continued hawkish Fed with a Dec. 9 hike priced could pressure equities and cap bond rallies.
Tech valuation and AI growth concerns are driving equity risk-off, with no clear incremental buyer.
Elevated UK inflation raises debt interest costs and fiscal pressure.
Iran escalation risk in the Strait of Hormuz could return a war-risk premium to oil.
Tech issuers paying high yields could crowd out the rest of credit.
TSMC's 44% weight makes Taiwan equities highly concentrated.
vol_and_positioning: VIX is at 29 after volatility jumped again in the US.
Hedge fund and systematic positioning is now very short, which limits the incremental seller base.
US gross exposure was flat and European GMV rose +1%, and there is little appetite to re-gross into year-end.
Gold has extreme CTA shorts but limited capitulation. Platinum forwards are tightening, signalling an emerging liquidity squeeze.
Fixed income positioning among systematic and discretionary accounts is not overly long, leaving capacity to rally.
geopolitical: Trump told Axios he will delay any decision on further strikes against Iran until the new year.
Iran intensified tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz through October and November, with at least two seafarers missing. The IEA said the war has 'permanently redrawn' global energy markets.
UK PM Burnham meets EU leaders in Brussels to advance the post-Brexit reset on agri-food, carbon markets and youth mobility.
Trump and Xi held talks in Shenzhen while Congress prepares a bill banning Chinese car sales in the US.
Marine Le Pen, frontrunner in next year's French election, promises to reverse the pension reform that raised the retirement age to 64.

tension_points.bull_case: Bonds are on a fifth straight session of gains with haven demand, and positioning is not overly long, leaving room to rally.
tension_points.bear_case: Hawkish Fedspeak, a priced 25bp December hike and inflation fears cap the upside and imply a structurally bearish outlook for Treasuries.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hawkish surprise from the Dec. 9 FOMC or equity stabilisation that removes haven demand.
